To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
genomic DNA can be isolated from minute quantities of fish scales and fins amenable to RAPDs.
the DNA extraction protocol from the minute quantities of live fish scale or fin tissue is highly effective and can be used for RAPD-PCR analysis.
the gDNA isolated from minute quantities of fish scales or fins is amenable for RAPD based genetic studies and that it is better to use live samples rather than frozen samples for isolation of gDNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a simple and rapid method for the extraction of high quality genomic DNA from small quantities of scales or fins of live fish.
the standardization of a non destructive method for gDNA isolation from minute quantities of fish scales and fins that can support RAPD PCR.
the standardization of a non-destructive sampling method for gDNA extraction from minute quantities of fish tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gDNAs isolated from live fish scales and fins could be used as templates for several rounds of RAMPD PCR and also for other molecular biology applications, which requires high quality gDNA.
the gDNAs isolated from scales or fin tissues of live fish are of superior quality
the gDNAs from minute quantity of scales and fins from live fish can be successfully isolated and used in RAPD-PCR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gDNA extraction protocol described in this work can be used for any species of fish, where the scales and fins are the only accessible tissues.
the present study provides an alternative method of sampling and a non destructive protocol of genomic DNA extraction for RAPD analysis from small fish samples.
the present protocol for extraction of gDNA from fish scales or fin tissues is simple, non destructive, cost effective and can be applied to a large number of fish species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scales and fin tissues can be used for gDNA isolation from live and fresh fish samples, without any harm to the fish.
the gDNA isolated from the scales or fin tissues of fishes can be used as templates in PCR based studies.
the scales and fins of live fishes can be used as a reliable source of genomic DNA for population genetic studies.
